newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe to enact law to protect AIDS sufferers.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe to enact law to protect AIDS sufferers.

text.p: Zimbabwe will next year gazette a national code of practice aimed at protecting people suffering from AIDS or infected with the HIV virus from discrimination, President Robert Mugabe said on Thursday.
He told parliament the code would outline the responsibilities of his government, employers and workers regarding people infected with the killer disease or the virus that causes it.

Zimbabwe has one of the highest rates of AIDS cases in Africa, with an estimated 10 percent of 10.5 million people estimated to have HIV. Health officials said earlier this year an average of 300 Zimbabweans were dying from the disease every week.
Although now prevalent, the disease is still socially stigmatised.

"In the face of growing unemployment, insecurity and discrimination faced by workers with HIV/AIDS, a national code of practice on AIDS and employment has been drafted after an extensive multi-sectoral consultative process and now awaits gazetting for it to become a statutory instrument to our Labour Relations Act," Mugabe said.
He said officially only 54,744 AIDS cases have been recorded since 1987, and that it was estimated that over 600,000 children would be orphaned by AIDS by the year 2000.
